narrator.instruct: Gripping, energetic storyteller telling a true Wild West heist, brisk and tense, never calm.

outlaw.instruct: A rough, impatient bank robber, menacing and loud.

heywood.instruct: A calm, stubborn bank cashier, quiet and steady, hiding his fear.

townsman.instruct: A shopkeeper shouting an alarm in the street, urgent and loud.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He told eight armed outlaws the bank safe was locked. It wasn't.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Northfield, Minnesota, eighteen seventy-six. The James-Younger gang rides into a quiet town.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Inside the bank sits acting cashier Joseph Heywood.

lines.speaker: heywood
lines.text: I can't. It's on a time lock.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The outlaws believe him. One steps into the vault, and Heywood throws the heavy door on him.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In the chaos, teller Alonzo Bunker bolts out the back door. A bullet hits his shoulder, but he keeps running.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Outside, the town has noticed. A hardware merchant grabs his rifle.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.text: Get your guns, boys! They're robbing the bank!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And inside, the outlaws are still waiting on a lock they think will never open.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You see, a time lock is a clock inside the safe door. Once it's set, nobody can open it until the hour comes.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But Heywood's clock had never been set. The safe was unlocked the whole time. One turn of the handle.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Bullets fill the street. The gang flees with twenty-six dollars and seventy cents.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Three outlaws were killed and three captured. The gang never recovered.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Heywood paid for his bluff with his life. But the bank's money never left the safe.
